page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-threaded scaling is limited, as shown by bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and PassMark CPU physics tests falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the bottom 10% tier, though cached small-block read bandwidth reaches 401.49 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity, this server offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that benefit from high single-thread burst performance but do not require sustained multi-core execution or large memory footprints. It is well-suited for lightweight web serving, basic Redis key-value operations, and running small-scale utility scripts or microservices. It is less suitable for database operations or memory-intensive applications due to its low memory score and weak database benchmark results.
